q: What is the difference between a static member and a normal (instance) member?
a: A static member belongs to the class (TestUser.DEFAULT_PASSWORD), shared once. An instance member belongs to each object (user.username).

q: What does `constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}` do?
a: It declares a private readonly property `page`, takes a parameter `page`, and assigns it (this.page = page). A shortcut for 3 lines.

q: Error: "Property 'name' has no initializer and is not definitely assigned in the constructor." Usual cause?
a: The property never gets a value. Often `name = name` instead of `this.name = name`. Assign it in the constructor or give it a default.

q: Error: "Value of type 'typeof Cart' is not callable. Did you mean to include 'new'?" Fix?
a: You called the class like a function: Cart(). Use new Cart().

q: Error: "Constructors for derived classes must contain a 'super' call." Fix?
a: In a class that extends another, call super(...) as the first line of the constructor, before using this.

q: Why does `items.forEach(cart.add)` crash with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'items')"?
a: forEach calls add on its own, without `cart.` in front, so `this` is undefined. Wrap it: (x) => cart.add(x).

q: Why do Playwright projects put pages in classes (Page Object Model)?
a: Locators and actions for a page live in one place. Tests read like steps (loginPage.login(...)), and when the page changes you fix one class, not 50 tests.
